title: The Fall of the Crown Prince
next_chapter_hook: The Crown Prince personally visited the location of Chen Ji's feigned death, requesting the 'Chen Ji Loyalists' to come to his aid—That door, will Chen Ji open it or not?

text.content: The fluctuations from the depths of the Tianji Record grow increasingly distinct. Chen Ji feels a sharp pain at his Brow Center—that blood-stained Jade Slip in his palm radiates intense heat, as if something desperately tries to break free. The lingering soul guardian Mo Xiansheng's voice emerges hauntingly: 'Young Master, the first page's restriction is already seventy percent lifted... An old friend awaits you.' Chen Ji's pupils slightly contract, yet he forcefully suppresses the surging emotions within, tucking the Jade Slip into his sleeve. This moment's peculiar movements from the Tianji Record are far from coincidental; the wheels of Heavenly Secrets have already begun to turn, and the news from the imperial court makes his brow furrow tightly—the Crown Prince's predicament has reached its most critical juncture.

At a teahouse on the outskirts of the Tianqing Sect, Chen Ji leans by the window, the clear tea before him has long gone cold. A gray-cloaked spy kneels on one knee, quietly reporting: 'Young Master, urgent news from the capital—Three days ago, the Second Prince launched an attack against the Crown Prince, purging three senior ministers from the Crown Prince's faction under the charge of 'conspiracy accomplices'. The Crown Prince's mansion is surrounded with no escape. Even the noble families who once allied with him have closed their doors and refused visitors.' Chen Ji's fingertips tap lightly on the table, his expression terrifyingly calm: 'What else?' The spy hesitates: 'The Second Prince is aggressively recruiting... your former subordinates, offering them the position of Deputy Secretary of the Secretariat.' Chen Ji's gaze turns ice-cold, yet a cold smile curves his lips—The Second Prince moves swiftly, but unfortunately, he's chosen the wrong direction.

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao has somehow appeared beside the window, her green garments fluttering dramatically in the wind. She coldly glances at the spy and waves him away before speaking: 'Chen Ji, your entire scheme is collapsing.' Chen Ji raises his eyes, unhurriedly lifting his cold tea for a sip: 'Su Senior Fellow's intelligence network is quite efficient.' Su Qingyao's brow furrows deeply: 'I'm worried about you! The Crown Prince's chess game was orchestrated by you. Now that his tree has fallen, the scattered monkeys will scatter—and your 'former subordinates'—' She pauses, her tone growing increasingly grave: 'Two have already defected to the Second Prince.' Chen Ji's hand playing with the teacup halts momentarily, a dangerous glint flashing in his eyes, yet he quickly regains composure: 'Understood.'

text.content: Seeing his nonchalant demeanor, Su Qingyao inexplicably feels a rising anger: 'What are you thinking? If the Crown Prince falls, your days at the Tianqing Sect won't be pleasant either. The Second Prince's next move will be to eliminate you—' Chen Ji suddenly looks up, those deep eyes like an abyss gazing directly into her heart: 'Su Senior Fellow, you seem quite concerned about me?' Su Qingyao chokes, her ear roots involuntarily flushing red, yet her tone hardens: 'I'm worried about the Sect! Do you think I don't know about your underhanded dealings?' Chen Ji laughs lightly, rises to his feet, walks to her, lowers his voice: 'Since you know, then there's even less reason to panic. The Second Prince wants my former subordinates? Let him have them. Chess pieces... while it's regrettable if they flee, their exposure is far more wasteful.'

Before the words finish, a shadow suddenly sweeps past the window. Su Qingyao instantly draws her sword, but Chen Ji presses her wrist: 'Don't move, it's one of ours.' The shadow lands and kneels—a black-clad woman with a light veil covering her face, her voice hoarse: 'Young Master, Her Highness the Princess has a secret letter for you.' Chen Ji takes the fragrant letter, unfolds it, and his gaze darkens instantly. The letter contains only a few words: 'Chen Ji is not dead, this Palace already knows. The capital's waters run deep, do not act hastily. In three days, at the Drunken Immortal Pavilion, come alone.—Mingyue.' Su Qingyao leans over for a glance, her expression shifting slightly: 'An imperial princess? How does she know you're not dead?'

choice.prompt: Princess Li Mingyue of the imperial court makes a covert move—what does she truly intend? Is she setting a trap to test, or does she harbor other schemes?

choices.text: Investigate the Princess's Intentions in Secret
choices.description: If the Princess could discover his feigned death, she must possess extraordinary abilities. First send someone to thoroughly investigate her trump cards, then make plans accordingly.
choices.visible_reward: Obtain More Intelligence on the Princess
choices.risk_hint: If the Princess genuinely wishes to recruit, delay might cause us to miss a golden opportunity

text.content: Chen Ji tucks the letter into his sleeve and speaks to the black-clad woman: 'Go back and tell your Princess, simply say that Chen Mou is already dead, and cannot accept the invitation.' The black-clad woman hesitates briefly, then obeys and departs. Su Qingyao frowns: 'Are you testing her?' Chen Ji shakes his head, his gaze profound: 'No, I'm waiting for her to reveal her hand. For the Princess to discover my feigned death, there must be someone behind her guiding... I want to see, which side does this noble lady from the deep palace truly stand on.'

However, the black-clad woman does not leave immediately. Instead, she retrieves a Jade Pendant from her bosom: 'The Princess said, if the Young Master doesn't believe, use this item to investigate a person—the newly appointed advisor in the Second Prince's residence, 'The Blue-Robed Wanderer'.' Chen Ji takes the Jade Pendant, his pupils constricting sharply—the patterns on that Jade Pendant are clearly Chen Family relics! 'She also said one more thing,' the black-clad woman lowers her voice: ''My sister asked me to deliver this.' Chen Ji's fingers tighten abruptly, the Tianji Record trembling violently in his Mental Sea—Chen Nian! Is his sister still alive?

choices.text: Proactively Meet Her to Ascertain the Truth
choices.description: Since the Princess dares to send an invitation, he dares to enter the game. This is the perfect opportunity to probe the trump cards of all parties in the imperial court.
choices.risk_hint: If the Princess Sets a Trap, One Might Never Return

text.content: Chen Ji ponders for a moment, then suddenly smiles: 'Interesting. Since the Princess has so graciously invited, how could Chen Mou disappoint?' Su Qingyao's face drains of color: 'Are you mad? What if it's a trap—' Chen Ji raises his hand to halt her words: 'Su Senior Fellow, why do you think the Crown Prince has managed to survive until now without being deposed?' He turns to gaze at the deepening twilight outside the window: 'Because someone is secretly protecting him. This chess game, the Princess began playing long ago.' Su Qingyao freezes, then clenches her teeth: 'Then I'm coming with you!' Chen Ji turns back, his gaze profound: 'Unnecessary. The Drunken Immortal Pavilion is a place of wine and women. If Su Senior Fellow goes, it would only alert the snake.'

Three days later, the Drunken Immortal Pavilion. Chen Ji, in blue robes, sits alone in an elegant room, the wine cup in his hand swaying with the candlelight. The door opens softly, and a graceful figure walks in gracefully—moon-white palace attire, high bun, precisely the imperial Princess Li Mingyue. After she settles, slender hands lift a wine pot, pouring Chen Ji a cup with a smile: 'Young Master Chen has great courage. This Palace thought you wouldn't dare come.' Chen Ji lifts the cup, drains it in one gulp, and says calmly: 'Since Your Highness summoned me, Chen Mou naturally had to come. I only wonder... what exactly does Your Highness wish to obtain from me?' The Princess purses her lips and smiles, yet a sharp glint flashes in those phoenix eyes: 'Chen Ji, how much do you think... your sister Chen Nian is worth as leverage?'

Meanwhile, in the Crown Prince's mansion in the capital. Crown Prince Li Chengqian sits alone in his study, memorials piled like mountains before him, yet he cannot read a single one. A servant hurries in to report: 'Your Highness, the Second Prince has struck again—he's spreading rumors throughout the city, claiming that Your Highness... has colluded with the Demonic Path, intending to rebel.' The Crown Prince hurls his teacup to the ground: 'Insolence!' He takes a deep breath, forces himself to remain calm, his gaze falling on a token hidden in a Secret Compartment of the bookcase—that is the only keepsake Chen Ji left him before departing. The Crown Prince mutters to himself: 'Chen Ji... are you dead or not? If you're dead, this chess game of mine... will truly be a dead game.'

Suddenly, commotion arises outside the study. The Crown Prince leaps to his feet, hand already on his sword hilt. However, a moment later, a familiar aged voice speaks: 'Your Highness, please don't panic, it's this old servant.' The Crown Prince relaxes, seeing a hunched old servant shuffle in, whispering near his ear: 'Your Highness, someone has delivered something.' With that, he presents a letter with no signature. The Crown Prince unfolds it, his pupils contracting sharply—there are only eight characters: 'In three days, the Drunken Immortal Pavilion, meet an old friend.' The handwriting is unmistakably Chen Ji's! The Crown Prince's hand trembles slightly, hope blazing in his eyes: 'Chen Ji... you truly are not dead!'

East of the capital city, the Second Prince's mansion. Night is deep, lanterns blaze brightly. Second Prince Li Chengze sits high on the main seat, before him kneeling several 'Chen Ji Loyalists' who have surrendered. He toys with a jade ring, a satisfied smile playing at his lips: 'Excellent. With Chen Ji dead, the Crown Prince is a tiger without fangs. Issue the command—continue the pressure. This Prince wants that Imperial Brother... before all the ministers and officials, to personally confess his crimes!' A strategist steps forward, whispering提醒: 'Your Highness, although Chen Ji's former subordinates have submitted, intelligence reports that the Crown Prince still seems to have contact with him...' The Second Prince coldly laughs: 'A dead man, what waves can he stir? Besides—' He lowers his voice, a ruthless glint flashing in his eyes: 'This Prince has already enlisted masters from the Xuanwu Sect. Even if Chen Ji isn't dead, if he dares to show himself, it's a dead end!'

choice.prompt: All factions are stirring restlessly—how will Chen Ji break the deadlock?

choices.description: Use the Tianji Record to foresight the trend within three shichen, confirming the Crown Prince and Princess's true intentions
choices.visible_reward: Learn the trend of key events within three shichen
choices.risk_hint: Heavenly Fate Value is precious, and may attract the notice of higher existences

text.content: Chen Ji returned to his dwelling, closed the doors and windows, and sat cross-legged. The Tianji Record emerged from his Mental Sea, its yellowed fragment slowly unfurling. Chen Ji closed his eyes in concentration, channeling a thread of spiritual consciousness into it. In an instant, the world before him twisted and transformed—he saw the Drunken Immortal Pavilion three shichen later, Crown Prince Li Chengqian sitting anxiously in an elegant room, yet the seat across from him remained empty; he saw the Second Prince feasting in celebration at his mansion, a squad of black-armored warriors scouring the city to hunt down Chen Ji's 'former subordinates'; finally, he saw the Moonlight Princess sitting alone in the deep palace, murmuring before a bronze mirror: 'Chen Nian... your brother is coming for you.' The vision shattered abruptly, and Chen Ji opened his eyes, cold sweat already beading on his forehead—the Tianji Record's foresight had never been so blurred, as if a layer of mist shrouded certain critical scenes.

Master Mo's voice rang in his mind, heavy with gravity: 'Young Master, while consuming Heavenly Fate Value, you must have noticed some visions becoming blurred.' Chen Ji said grimly: 'Chen Nian?' Master Mo was silent for a moment: 'The existence of the Heavenly Fate Lock will interfere with foresight. Young Master, your sister... may have awakened some of her power.' Chen Ji's fists clenched white. Master Mo continued: 'There is one more thing this old servant must tell you—the 'Blue-Robed Guest' the Princess mentioned is precisely the descendant of the one who betrayed the Chen family back then. His hiding by the Second Prince's side is no coincidence.' A cold gleam flashed in Chen Ji's eyes: 'I've noted it.'

choices.text: Hold position and observe the changing situation
choices.description: Since the Tianji Record has already given warnings, it means there are too many variables. Better to use stillness to overcome motion, letting the enemy reveal their weaknesses first
choices.visible_reward: Preserve strength and assess the situation clearly
choices.risk_hint: If the Crown Prince cannot hold on, the entire scheme will completely collapse

text.content: Chen Ji ultimately chose to wait. He summoned his trusted spies and set up three contingency plans: first, strictly monitor the movements of the Second Prince's mansion and the Crown Prince's mansion; second, investigate the true identity of the 'Blue-Robed Guest' and his connection to the Chen family; third, secretly protect those 'former subordinates' who have not yet defected to the enemy, and if necessary, expose one or two insignificant pawns in exchange for crucial intelligence. After the deployment was complete, Chen Ji stood with hands clasped behind his back at the window, gazing toward the direction of the Imperial Capital, his eyes deep and unfathomable: 'The Second Prince wants to use my people? Fine, let him use them. When he becomes accustomed to relying on them, then suddenly pull them away—that is when the real pain begins.'

However, no plan survives contact with the changing situation. Late the second night, shocking news that shook the Imperial Capital arrived—Crown Prince Li Chengqian was impeached by the Second Prince on charges of 'colluding with the Demonic Path and plotting rebellion.' The Emperor flew into a rage and ordered a public confrontation at the Taihe Hall in three days! When the news reached Chen Ji, he was drinking tea, and the cup in his hand trembled slightly. Su Qingyao burst in, her face deathly pale: 'Chen Ji, the Crown Prince is finished! The confrontation in three days is obviously a Hongmen Banquet!' Chen Ji slowly set down his teacup, a sharp gleam flashing in his eyes: 'No, it's not over yet.' He rose, his tone平静得近乎冷酷：'是时候……让某些人知道，什么叫扮猪吃虎了。'

News from the Imperial Capital poured in like snowflakes. Chen Ji received urgent reports: the Second Prince not only impeached the Crown Prince for treason but also presented testimonies from three witnesses in court—all former trusted confidants of the Crown Prince, now unanimously accusing the Crown Prince of colluding with the Demonic Path. As the entire court erupted in outrage, the Second Prince struck another heavy blow: 'Your Majesty, I have another piece of evidence—the Crown Prince's ability to command the court is entirely due to guidance from 'Chen Ji,' the very person who stirred up trouble three years ago! Unfortunately, this man died a few months ago, with no one to contest the charges. Your Highness... do you dare let me continue investigating?' In the court, absolute silence. Crown Prince Li Chengqian's face turned ashen, his lips trembling, yet he could not utter a single word.

dialogue.content: Meanwhile, in a secret chamber on the outskirts of the Tianqing Sect, Chen Ji looked at the detailed court memorial in his hand, a mocking smile curling at the corner of his lips. He handed the memorial to Su Qingyao and said calmly: 'Su Senior Fellow, what do you think of the Second Prince's article? How well was it written?' Su Qingyao glanced through it, her expression growing increasingly grave: 'Reversing black and white, pressing step by step... this memorial is beautifully written, but even more impressive are his three witnesses.' Chen Ji nodded: 'Indeed. Buying three people to betray their old master, promising high positions and great wealth—this approach... isn't it familiar?' Su Qingyao was stunned, then understood—the Second Prince was clearly copying Chen Ji's own tactics from years past! Chen Ji sneered: 'Unfortunately, he only learned the surface.'

text.content: Chen Ji rose and walked to the desk, spreading out a blank sheet of paper and dipping his brush in ink. Su Qingyao leaned over to look and saw him write four names, circle three, and draw an X: 'My three 'former subordinates,' after defecting to the Second Prince, their first mission was to provide false testimony. They thought they were being promoted, but little did they know... this was merely the first step toward becoming discarded pieces.' Su Qingyao frowned: 'Do you mean the Second Prince will eliminate the witnesses?' Chen Ji set down his brush and turned to face her: 'Not 'will,' but 'already has.' He drew a secret letter from his sleeve: 'News that came half an hour ago—all three died tonight. The cause of death was 'suicide from guilt.' Su Qingyao gasped: 'The Second Prince has a ruthless heart!' Chen Ji said calmly: 'Not ruthless, but fearful. He fears these people, if kept, will eventually become a future trouble.'

choice.prompt: The Second Prince killed the witnesses and destroyed evidence—how should Chen Ji exploit this flaw to counterattack?

choices.text: Turn the tables and lure the snake out of its hole
choices.description: Have the remaining former subordinates deliberately expose their whereabouts, luring the Second Prince to send people to kill them, then present the evidence to the Emperor
choices.visible_reward: The Second Prince's crime of murdering witnesses will be established
choices.risk_hint: If the Second Prince notices, he will strike first

text.content: Chen Ji wrote several secret orders and handed them to his trusted aide: 'Deliver my words to the surviving former subordinates—tonight at the Hour of Hai, exit the city through three hidden gates on the east side, moving slowly, slow enough for the Second Prince's men to catch up.' Su Qingyao was puzzled: 'Are you sending them to their deaths?' Chen Ji shook his head: 'No, I'm fishing. Since the Second Prince dared to murder witnesses, he certainly dares to send pursuers. Who the pursuers are, how many, who leads them—these are the key points.' A faint smile played at the corner of his mouth: 'On the court assembly three days later, the Second Prince thinks he holds certain victory. Little does he know, the real ironclad evidence... is tonight.'

Su Qingyao watched Chen Ji methodically laying out his plans, then suddenly spoke up: "Chen Ji, I find you increasingly unfathomable." Chen Ji raised an eyebrow: "Oh?" Su Qingyao said seriously: "You know full well how dangerous the Crown Prince's situation is, yet I've never seen you truly worried. Even as the Second Prince presses closer, you always appear supremely confident... What exactly are you waiting for?" Chen Ji fell silent for a moment, then turned to gaze out the window at the night: "I'm waiting for someone." Su Qingyao pressed further: "Who?" Chen Ji didn't answer, but his gaze越过重重宫阙，落在皇都深处某个方向——那里，正是太子府的所在。 He lowered his voice: "If the Crown Prince truly possesses the qualities of an enlightened ruler, he won't just sit and wait for death. At the court assembly three days from now... he will stake everything. And that, that's when we truly see who emerges victorious."

choices.text: Meet the Crown Prince directly to propose a strategy
choices.description: Infiltrate the Crown Prince's manor under cover of darkness, lay out the entire plan, and join forces with the Crown Prince for a counterattack.
choices.visible_cost: Exposing my whereabouts greatly increases the risk
choices.visible_reward: Establish genuine trust with the Crown Prince
choices.risk_hint: The Crown Prince's surroundings may harbor the Second Prince's spies

text.content: That night at the hour of the rat, Chen Ji infiltrated the Crown Prince's manor alone. The guards, seeing it was him, were both startled and delighted, quickly leading him to the inner chambers. Crown Prince Li Chengqian sat beneath the lamp, gaunt and hollow, and when he saw Chen Ji enter, he nearly burst into tears: "Chen Ji! You... you truly aren't dead!" Chen Ji knelt on one knee: "Your Highness, forgive me. My feigned death had other secrets." The Crown Prince personally helped him up: "Rise quickly! Between us, such formalities are unnecessary! During this time, this prince has been like a stray dog, abandoned by all the officials in the court..." Chen Ji stared directly into his eyes: "Does Your Highness have confidence to survive the court assembly three days from now?" The Crown Prince苦笑："This prince... is already at the end of my strength." Chen Ji said沉声道："Then let's turn the tables. This subject has a strategy that can make the Second Prince... lose everything."

Chen Ji laid out his entire plan: First, gather evidence of the Second Prince's murder and silencing of witnesses; second, make a counterattack at the court assembly; third, ask Princess Mingyue to testify—she is not opposed to the Crown Prince as everyone believes, but has secretly formed an alliance with him. The Crown Prince's eyes blazed with excitement after hearing this: "Excellent! Excellent indeed, turning the tables! Chen Ji, this prince truly did not misjudge you!" Chen Ji then泼了一盆冷水："Your Highness, if this plan succeeds, the Crown Prince's throne can be preserved; but if it fails..." The Crown Prince interrupted him, standing up with determined eyes: "Chen Ji, this prince's life was never intended to be kept anyway. Rather than sitting and waiting for death, we might as well risk it all!"

As their secret meeting ended, dawn was breaking in the east. The Crown Prince personally escorted Chen Ji out of the manor, whispering before parting: "Chen Ji, this prince has one request." Chen Ji paused: "Please speak, Your Highness." The Crown Prince took a deep breath: "Princess Mingyue... she is my sister from the same mother, but because our mother died early, she was despised by our father. All these years she's navigated the palace with every step like walking on thorns, and this prince was powerless to protect her. Now she's risked great danger to send you that letter, truly wanting to help us. If you see her..." Chen Ji淡淡道："Your Highness can rest assured. Chen Ji treats kindness and grudges with clarity. If the Princess truly assists me, I certainly won't wrong her." The Crown Prince exhaled in relief, watching Chen Ji's silhouette disappear into the morning mist. In the distance, the gates of the Crown Prince's manor slowly closed, and a new round of scheming had just begun.

However, variables always exceed plans. Just as Chen Ji returned to his lodging, Mo Xiansheng's voice arose in his Mental Sea: "Young Master, something terrible has happened." Chen Ji's brow furrowed: "What happened?" Mo Xiansheng's voice carried grave weight: "This old servant just sensed that the seal on the third page of the Tianji Record... loosened by itself." Chen Ji's heart clenched—the third page was precisely the one recording the 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key.' He immediately pressed: "Is it because of Chen Nian?" Mo Xiansheng沉默片刻："Perhaps it's not just that. The Eyes of Heavenly Dao... it may have already noticed you." Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply, the Tianji Record trembled slightly in his Mental Sea, as if responding to some indescribable gaze. He took a deep breath, suppressing the churning emotions in his heart,低声："It seems this game... is larger than I imagined."

Three days later, the Taihe Hall Court Assembly. All the officials of the court gathered, Second Prince Li Chengze was triumphant and confident, while Crown Prince Li Chengqian's face was ashen. However, just as the Second Prince prepared to present the final piece of 'ironclad evidence' before the throne, a commotion suddenly arose outside the hall. An attendant rushed into the hall, kneeling and announcing loudly: "Reporting to Your Majesty—the Crown Prince has a petition to present! Additionally... Princess Mingyue requests an audience!" The Emperor on the dragon throne furrowed his brow, his gaze sweeping across the officials below, finally landing on the Crown Prince. The Crown Prince took a deep breath and stepped forward: "Father, this son has grievances to申诉!" The Second Prince冷笑："Imperial Brother, didn't all your so-called witnesses die by committing suicide out of guilt? What more could you possibly—" Before he finished speaking, the hall doors burst open, and Princess Mingyue Li Mingyue walked gracefully in wearing plain white garments, holding a sandalwood box in her hands. Her gaze was like a blade, striking directly at the Second Prince: "Second Imperial Brother, please don't be in such a hurry. Though the witnesses are dead... the evidence of the murderer's crimes remains."

In the court above, the atmosphere instantly froze. The Second Prince's expression changed slightly, but he强行镇定："Mingyue, what do you mean by this?" Princess Mingyue opened the sandalwood box, inside which赫然是三具焦黑的骨灰盒，以及一份染血的遗书："These are the three witnesses who 'died by suicide out of guilt.' Second Imperial Brother's methods are admirable—murder and silencing witnesses, yet remembering to falsify the scene. Unfortunately—" She took a token from her sleeve: "The assassins Second Imperial Brother sent were from the Xuanwu Sect. This token was found on one of those assassins." The entire court erupted in uproar! The Second Prince's face turned ashen: "You—you're slandering me!" Princess Mingyue冷笑："Whether it's slander or not, His Majesty's wise judgment will determine the truth." The Emperor took the token, his gaze deep as he glanced at the Second Prince—a look that made the Second Prince feel as if he had fallen into an icy abyss.

Chen Ji did not appear in the court hall—he had already anticipated what would happen on this day. At this moment, he stood on a hillside outside the Imperial Capital, gazing toward the direction of the Taihe Hall from afar. Su Qingyao stood beside him, frowning: "Since you've orchestrated everything to this point, why not witness the Second Prince's downfall in person?" Chen Ji stood with hands clasped behind his back,淡淡道："What's there to see? His fate was sealed the moment he decided to move against the Crown Prince." Su Qingyao沉默片刻，忽然道："Chen Ji, you scheme across the realm, leaving nothing to chance... but have you ever considered what happens if you miscalculate one day?" Chen Ji turned to look at her, his gaze profound: "Then I'd have to accept my fate." He paused, then added: "However, before I accept my fate—" His gaze越过层层宫阙，落在某个不可知的方向："I want everyone who wants me dead... to enter the grave before me."

Su Qingyao gazed at his profile, suddenly feeling that this man before her was both familiar and unfamiliar. She opened her mouth, wanting to say something, but was interrupted by Chen Ji: "Chief Su, I know what you want to ask." He收回目光，望向远方渐渐散去的晨雾："You want to ask if all of this is worth it? You want to ask what I'm scheming across the realm for? You want to ask about my sister's whereabouts?" Su Qingyao怔住，点了点头。 Chen Ji沉默良久，方才开口："I might as well tell you." He turned around, for the first time正视她的眼睛，that pair of eyes profound as an abyss, yet showing a rare trace of exhaustion: "I scheme across the realm, not for power, not for immortality—I only want to find Chen Nian. Then, take her away from this people-devouring place." He paused,补充道："As for now... it's time to keep an appointment." Su Qingyao pressed: "What appointment?" Chen Ji's lips curved slightly, forming a meaningful smile: "Someone has come to call, and I must go... see an old friend."
